blocks.text: As Japan faces a severe labor shortage in many sectors such as healthcare and manufacturing, more companies are counting on artificial intelligence-driven robots, paving the way for them to play a greater role in the workplace. The Japanese government has set a target of introducing 10 million AI-powered robots by 2040 to deal with the labor shortage caused by the country’s aging and shrinking population. In August, AI startup Zeals Co. unveiled its D1 wheeled humanoid robot at a launch event in Tokyo.
